Long, thin, and hanging limply — without fullness, bounce, or body.

1. Describing hair

This is where "lank" is used most often. Lank hair is straight, flat, and lifeless — it just hangs down without any volume, curl, or energy. Think of hair that lies completely flat against the head, perhaps slightly greasy or thin, with no bounce or movement to it. It doesn't wave, it doesn't curl, it doesn't lift. It simply droops.

"She pushed her lank hair away from her face."
"After hours in the rain, his hair hung in lank, wet strands."

The word suggests not just straightness but a kind of limpness — as if the hair has given up. It's slightly negative in tone. "Straight hair" is neutral; "lank hair" has a faint sense of dullness or neglect about it.

2. Describing a person or body part

When used for a person, "lank" means tall and thin — but in a way that looks somewhat ungainly or hollow, not in a graceful or athletic way. A lank person is thin to the point where their height makes them look stretched out and bony.

"A lank young man unfolded himself from the chair."
"His lank frame barely filled the oversized coat."

When used for specific body parts — fingers, limbs, a neck — it means long and thin, with a slightly lifeless or frail quality.

"She had lank, pale fingers that wrapped easily around the glass."

"Lank" always implies an absence of something — of fullness, of life, of vitality. Something lank is not robustly solid or richly textured. It is reduced, flat, thin. That's why it tends to carry a slightly melancholy or unflattering tone, even when used neutrally.

Compare it to related words:

  • Lean = simply thin (neutral, sometimes even admirable)
  • Lanky = tall and thin with an awkward, ungainly quality (very similar to lank for people — in fact, lanky comes from lank)
  • Limp = lacking stiffness or energy (focuses on limpness, not thinness)
  • Lank = the combination: thin and hanging limply, without body or energy
Lank means long and thin in a flat, lifeless, drooping way — most often describing hair that hangs without volume or curl, or a person/limb that is tall and thinly hollow-looking.
